narration.text: Feed Control Lab: natural-language control of a short-video recommender on real KuaiRec data. A trained SASRec model ranks; the language model only proposes, and I review.
First, the original study. Condition C takes a free-text category instruction.
I name one category by its dataset ID.
Apply. The rule parser reads it, and the fixed policy boosts that category.
Now the language controls.
Everything here is English: the KuaiRec text was machine-translated before processing, and the models read the English text.
On the right: this user's top ten from the trained model.
Provider: the OpenAI API.
Model: GPT five mini, fast and inexpensive, and the best of my tests at new categories.
Reasoning effort low, the same setting as the measured results.
This is where your own API key goes. I paste mine into the masked field.
Use this provider. The key stays in this server's memory only; it is never shown, logged or saved.
The status line confirms it: key typed into this page, memory only.
Workflow one, the reference: a manual category control. No model.
This user's feed is full of news and incident stories, so first I hide those categories.
I search for incident.
Labels can be searched in English.
I pick Social incident.
I pick Legal incident.
I search for news.
Labels can be searched in English.
I pick Social news.
I pick Livelihood news.
I search for disaster.
Labels can be searched in English.
I pick Disaster accident.
The action is Hide.
Preview. A preview never changes the feed.
Five hide controls: 493 videos would leave the feed, and 5 leave the top ten.
Apply changes exactly the reviewed set. These stay applied for the rest of this video.
The news and incident categories are now listed under Applied now.
Now one more: dance.
I search for dance.
I pick Dance.
Show more,
strong.
Preview.
10 dance videos would enter the top ten.
Apply.
Each card names the control that moved it.
Undo removes the dance boost and restores the previous feed exactly; the news hide stays.
Workflow two: a request in my own words, mapped to existing categories and tags.
I just ate, and do not want to be tempted by food.
No category name is used.
Interpret and preview.
The model reads the request and the list of existing labels. It sees no video text.
The answer is back.
Proposal: hide category Snack; hide category Food tutorial. 1 model call, 6 seconds of model time, less than one cent.
Apply.
Undo.
A second request, in another domain.
My cat is at the vet, and I cannot bear to see animals.
No category name is used.
Interpret and preview.
The model reads the request and the list of existing labels. It sees no video text.
Next, the server checks that every label exists and that the quoted words are in the request.
The answer is back.
Proposal: hide category Pet cat; hide category Pet dog; hide category Pets; hide category Pet daily record, and 10 more. 1 model call, 7 seconds of model time, less than one cent.
Apply.
Undo.
Workflow three: a new category that KuaiRec does not have.
I describe it.
Plain English, no existing label.
The scope is the top fifty videos of this user's current feed; the hidden news videos are left out.
Step one: propose a definition.
The model reads the description and the top videos of this user's current feed.
It drafts a label and a definition, and cites example videos with exact quotations.
The answer is back.
A label, a definition with conditions, and 4 cited examples, each quotation checked.
I review it, and shorten the label.
When applied: show more.
Approve and classify.
Each video in scope is classified under the definition, ten per call, four calls in parallel.
Every match must quote the video's own text.
A separate call checks each quotation without seeing the verdict.
Only matches that pass both checks are selected.
Still waiting for the model, 21s so far.
Still waiting for the model, 27s so far.
The answer is back.
One row per video: verdict, quotation, independent check. 3 of 50 selected. 6 model calls, 76 seconds of model time, about 1 cents.
The feed stays visible on the right during review.
Apply. The new category is now a label of its own.
2 of its videos enter the top ten, and its members move up.
Workflow four: add a video that is not in KuaiRec.
A title
and
a description.
The model sees only these words.
Classify and preview.
The model assigns existing categories and tags, and judges the new category with a quotation.
The answer is back.
It got existing categories and tags. For my new category: a match, with a quotation and a passed independent check, so it joins the category.
Apply. It starts at this user's median score, since the recommender has no history for it, so it does not reach the top ten by itself.
Undo removes the new video; the new category and its members stay.
The Results page reads the measured result files. I will go through the headline numbers.
These numbers were measured on the original-text run of 17 November. The re-run on the English text is pending.

The first table is the nonliteral requests. Exact means the right action, every required label, and nothing outside the reviewed acceptable set. Claude Sonnet five point five 17 of 20; GPT five 17 of 20; GPT five mini 16 of 20; Llama three point one eight B 0 of 20; Qwen two point five coder seven B 0 of 20.

Next, cases where the model should not change the feed. Correct abstentions: Claude Sonnet five point five 12 of 14; GPT five 10 of 14; GPT five mini 7 of 14; Llama three point one eight B 11 of 14; Qwen two point five coder seven B 9 of 14.

For new categories, member F1 on the shared pool of one hundred fifty KuaiRec items: Claude Sonnet five point five 0.87; GPT five 0.92; GPT five mini 0.94; Llama three point one eight B 0.18; Qwen two point five coder seven B 0.47.

Local versus frontier: the local models matched 0 and 0 of 20 nonliteral requests; where they proposed almost nothing, their abstention scores, 11 and 9 of 14, reflect refusing, not judgement. The frontier models matched 16 to 17 of 20. Local calls cost nothing, but took 126 and 109 seconds each at the median on this laptop.

Finally, the old one-hundred-case parser bank, re-used and labelled as re-use, scored strictly: Llama three point one eight B 79; Qwen two point five coder seven B 74; GPT five mini 60; GPT five 60 out of one hundred. None reaches the eighty-five percent target.
The test set was drafted by an AI and reviewed row by row by me. Claude is both the drafter's family and a measured model.
Code, tests, data and results are in the repository. Thank you.
